title: Q4-2025 & FY2026 goals + self-review notes
content:
Quick brain dump for upcoming 1:1 and performance write-up. Mostly notes to self - messy.

Current context:
- role: Senior People Ops Partner (supporting eng + product orgs).
- focus last 6 months: hiring scale for infra + serving-runtime, compensation redesign pilot, onboarding flow improvements.
- headcount: supported 42 hires (offer -> start) across Q2-Q3 2025; goal was 35, so exceeded.

Top wins (metrics + concrete outcomes):
- Hiring velocity: reduced average time-to-offer from 26 -> 18 days for SWE IC roles (ref: JIRA HR-1423). Quick notes on what worked: standardized interview packet, hiring manager playbook (PR#88), weekly sync w/ talent partners.
- Comp pilot: ran 6-team pilot for banding + ranges; got exec buy-in for rollout plan. Saved ~12% overcomp by tightening ranges & removing inconsistent overrides.
- Onboarding: shipped onboarding checklist + slack bot reminders for first 30 days - increased new hire 30-day engagement survey score from 72 -> 81.
- Process docs: consolidated interview guides into single Confluence space; reduced duplicate scheduling errors (tracked in spreadsheet attached to confluence page).

Areas to improve / gaps:
- Manager enablement: still reactive. Need proactive manager training > create 90-min "manager bootcamp" template (deliverable for Q2 FY2026).
- Analytics: org-level dashboards are still manual. Need to get HRIS to automate monthly headcount attrition dashboard. Open ticket: HRIS-210.
- Diversity hiring: pipeline improving but conversion rate at onsites -> offers is lower for underrepresented candidates. Root-cause hypothesis: interview rubrics not calibrated consistently. Action: run 2 calibration sessions in next 60 days with hiring managers.

Promotion / career conversation prep (notes for manager):
- Case for promotion to People Ops Manager:
  - Impact: drove hiring capacity for infra org at scale (42 hires) while improving quality of hire metrics (day-90 performance flagged as meeting/exceeding expectations for 86% of hires).
  - Ownership: led compensation pilot from scoping -> rollout recommendation, cross-functional with finance and legal.
  - Leadership: mentored 2 junior recruiters and paired with TA lead on sourcing strategy.
  - Readiness: feel ready to own a small people ops pod (2 ICs + 1 contractor).
- Evidence to include in packet: offer rate improvements, comp pilot summary, testimonial from Eng hiring manager (Ravi P), snapshot of onboarding NPS uplift (confluence link).
- Risks / counter-arguments I expect:
  - "Need more experience running a team" - plan: propose 6-month acting lead for hiring ops to show direct management experience.
  - "Focus is too hiring-heavy; need broader HR ops experience" - plan: volunteer to own benefits vendor RFP and HRIS automation project.

Talking points for 1:1 with manager (Maya):
- 1) Quick run-through of Q4 wins & metrics (2-3 slides / bullets).
- 2) Ask: support for promotion packet + suggested timeline (goal: decision by end of Q2 FY2026).
- 3) Ask: interim stretch assignment - lead HRIS dashboard automation and 90-day manager bootcamp.
- 4) Coaching asks: feedback on cross-functional influence, stakeholder mgmt with finance. Specific feedback examples I want: where I could be more assertive vs collaborative.

Concrete next steps (mini checklist):
- [ ] Draft promotion packet (include metrics + comp pilot summary + 2 manager testimonials) - target: 2026-03-10.
- [ ] Book calibration sessions for interviewers - target: 2026-03-20.
- [ ] Draft manager bootcamp agenda and pilot with one eng manager - target: 2026-04-01.
- [ ] Open HRIS automation scoping doc + link to HRIS-210.
- [ ] Ask Maya to sponsor 6-month acting lead assignment.

Unresolved / questions to think about:
- Is the promotion better positioned as individual contributor seniorization vs manager track? Pros/cons.
- How to quantify "quality of hire" in a way that won't be dismissed as noisy - think combining 30-day engagement + 90-day perf flags + hiring manager satisfaction survey.
- Should I include a list of 3 stretch hires I want to own as part of the promotion ask? (good signal of ramp plan).

Notes to self (phrases & snippets to paste into packet):
- "Scale without compromising quality: standardized interview packets and calibration reduced variance and improved time-to-offer."
- "Built cross-functional partners in finance/legal to design a compensation pilot that preserved competitiveness while improving consistency."
- "Led onboarding changes that measurably improved early-employee engagement scores."

Quick links / artifacts to attach to packet (copy into confluence):
- Confluence: PeopleOps/2025-Comp-Pilot-summary (attachment: comp-brief.pdf)
- JIRA: HR-1423 (hiring velocity improvements)
- Slack thread: #eng-hiring "Ravi: offer feedback" (link)
- Spreadsheet: hiring-velocity-q2-q3-2025.csv

Style / tone notes for packet (internal): keep it concise, evidence-first, put the ask up front (promotion request + timeline). Include 1 page summary + appendix of metrics.

Misc scratch ideas:
- run "interview calibration lunch" (brown-bag) with snack budget to increase attendance.
- pilot peer interviewing training where high-perf ICs pair with new interviewers.

End of notes.

(Will polish into formal promotion packet doc after 1:1 - this is the working draft and todo list.)
